title: Period of Rental under Rental Reimbursement Coverage
content:
Under Rental Reimbursement Coverage the period for which rental days are paid opens and closes on the dates set out here. The same dates and counts apply under every Cardinal Point Rental Reimbursement package ($20/$600, $25/$750, $30/$900, $40/$1,200, $50/$1,500 and $60/$1,800).

## First rental day

| Kind of loss | First rental day |
|---|---|
| A loss other than theft | The date the vehicle is left at the repair facility, or the date of loss when the vehicle is not drivable |
| Theft | Rental for a stolen vehicle starts once 48 elapsed hours have passed after the theft is reported to the company |

## Last rental day

| Outcome | Last rental day |
|---|---|
| Vehicle repaired | The day the repair facility reports the vehicle ready |
| Total loss | Rental days are still paid for 3 days after the day the total loss settlement offer is made; the date that starts these days is the date the settlement offer is made to the named insured |
| Stolen vehicle recovered undamaged | The day after recovery |
| Stolen vehicle recovered damaged | The day the repair facility reports the vehicle ready |

## Counting rental days

- Rental days are counted as calendar days from the pick-up date through the day before return.
- Any part of a calendar day counts as one day.

## Worked dates (hypothetical)

- **Total loss.** The settlement offer is made to the named insured on a hypothetical day T. The 3 extra days are the three days after day T: T plus one, T plus two and T plus three. The day after those three is not paid as an extra day.
- **Theft.** A theft is reported to the company at a hypothetical moment on day D. The 48 elapsed hours run out on day D plus two, at the same time of day as the report.
- **Recovery.** A stolen vehicle is recovered undamaged on a hypothetical day R. Its last rental day is R plus one. Had it been recovered damaged, the last rental day would instead be the day the repair facility reports it ready.
